headline: half the September fall has come back, and this time 2027 led the rise
commentary: UK power spot is 151.70 £/MWh, up 6.5% since our last update on 22 September and 81% higher than a year ago. The gas front month, now November, is 189.74 p/therm, so half of the late-September fall has already come back. The drivers are familiar: continued attacks on tanker traffic in the Middle East, higher shipping insurance, and European storage at 72% full, up from 66% a month ago but still well short of where it normally sits going into winter. What has changed is where the rise landed. Last time the fall was concentrated in this winter while 2027 barely moved. This time 2027 rose faster: Summer 27 is up 14.5% and Winter 27 up 10.9%, against 5 to 9% for the winter months ahead. Winter 27 at 137.50 has broken above the 124 to 130 range it held through September, and Summer 27 now trades above it, which is the market pricing in an expensive storage refill next year. That matters because the cheaper end of the curve is what makes a longer contract attractive. A 12-month contract starting in November is about 1.03 p/kWh higher on a wholesale-equivalent basis than two weeks ago, a 24-month about 0.90 p/kWh. The 24-month still sits around 16% below the 12-month, so term still wins. But the window we flagged last time has largely closed, and waiting is now costing money across the whole curve.

gas.note: NBP front-month is now Nov 26 at 189.74 p/therm (Oct 26 has gone into delivery), up 5.4% on its 22 Sep print of 179.96 and half way back to its 18 Sep level of 199.45. The rest of this winter: Dec 26 192.88, Jan 27 194.08, Feb 27 193.28, Mar 27 183.60, Q1 27 189.25. Unlike the last three editions, the move is led by the back of the curve: Summer 27 144.50 (+14.5%), Winter 27 137.50 (+10.9%), Summer 28 89.00 (+10.2%). Winter 27 has broken above the 123.75-130.25 range it held across five readings, and Summer 27 now prices above Winter 27, a refill premium for a storage season starting from a low base. The step-down still makes the case for term: Q1 27 189.25 to Winter 27 137.50 is a 27.3% discount (28.9% on 22 Sep), and Summer 28 at 89.00 is a further step below. A 24-month contract still blends this winter down with cheaper 2027 and 2028, but 2027 is no longer the stable anchor it was.
